title: Sourdough Discard Cinnamon Raisin English Muffins

ingredients: Cornmeal or semolina flour for dusting
directions: Mix warm milk, melted butter, sourdough discard, brown sugar, and yeast in a large mixing bowl and let sit a few minutes. Add flours, salt, and cinnamon and mix with a dough whisk or wooden spoon until a slightly sticky dough forms.
Add raisins and continue mixing until all ingredients are thoroughly combined.
Scrape sides of bowl, cover, and let rise until doubled — about 60–90 minutes.
OPTIONAL: Refrigerate dough overnight to develop flavors. Proceed with step 5 the next day.

After dough has doubled (or after chilling overnight), dump onto a floured surface and press or roll out to about 1-inch thickness. Cut rounds with a 3-inch biscuit cutter or drinking glass. Reshape scraps by stacking, re-rolling, and cutting. Aim for 9–12 muffins.
Place muffins on a pan lined heavily with cornmeal or semolina flour. Dust both sides well. Cover and let rise for about 1 hour until puffy and light.

Preheat an electric skillet to 300°F or a heavy skillet over medium-low heat. Place risen muffins in, leaving space. Cover and cook for 5–7 minutes. Flip and cook on the second side for another 5–7 minutes, covered. Reduce heat to 200–250°F and flip a few more times until internal temperature reads 195–200°F.
Remove to a cooling rack and cool to room temperature. Use a fork to pry the halves apart for the best craggy nooks and crannies.

notes: For best nooks and crannies, use a fork and your fingers to pry the halves apart before toasting.
